metadata.name: [GCP Compute OTel] CPU steal from host contention
metadata.description: Alerts when VMs in a zone spend at least 10% of their vCPU time ready to run but not scheduled by the hypervisor (CPU steal, from scheduler_wait_time) over 15 minutes. Shared-core VMs, which are throttled by design, are excluded. Returns one row per affected project and zone.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.compute.otel-*
// Compute Engine VM instances only
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
// scheduler_wait_time is a DELTA metric stored as a gauge: seconds of wait in each 60s sample,
// accumulated across all vCPUs. Never use RATE().
// OTel TSDS can split one entity's history into several series (_metric_names_hash is a dimension).
// Collapse to one row per minute first, then: means = SUM(sums) / SUM(counts); latest value = LAST(x, minute).
| STATS
    wait_sum = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/scheduler_wait_time`)),
    wait_n = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/scheduler_wait_time`)),
    vcpus = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/guest_visible_vcpus`)),
    reserved_cores = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/reserved_cores`))
  BY minute = TBUCKET(1 minute), resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, resource.attributes.instance_id, attributes.instance_name
| STATS
    wait_sum = SUM(wait_sum),
    wait_n = SUM(wait_n),
    vcpus = LAST(vcpus, minute) WHERE vcpus IS NOT NULL,
    reserved_cores = LAST(reserved_cores, minute) WHERE reserved_cores IS NOT NULL
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, resource.attributes.instance_id, attributes.instance_name
// Exclude shared-core VMs (reserved cores < visible vCPUs): their wait time reflects intentional throttling.
| WHERE wait_n > 0 AND vcpus > 0 AND reserved_cores >= vcpus
// Mean wait seconds per minute, as a percentage of total vCPU time available in a minute
| EVAL wait_s_per_min = TO_DOUBLE(wait_sum) / wait_n
| EVAL steal_pct = wait_s_per_min * 100.0 / (60.0 * vcpus)
// Per-VM steal threshold (%). 10% sustained is significant contention; lower to 5% for latency-sensitive fleets.
| EVAL is_affected = steal_pct >= 10
| STATS
    affected_instances = COUNT(*) WHERE is_affected,
    instances = COUNT(*),
    max_steal_pct = ROUND(MAX(steal_pct), 2),
    affected_instance_names = VALUES(attributes.instance_name) WHERE is_affected
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone

breach.segment:
// Breach: at least 1 VM in the zone is affected. Raise to require a zone-wide pattern (host overcommit wave).
WHERE affected_instances >= 1
| KEEP resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, affected_instances, instances, max_steal_pct, affected_instance_names
| SORT max_steal_pct DESC
| LIMIT 50

data.content:
## CPU steal from host contention

One or more VMs in this zone are losing at least 10% of their vCPU time waiting for the hypervisor to schedule them (`instance/cpu/scheduler_wait_time`). This is host-level contention, not a workload problem: the guest is ready to run but the physical host is not giving it CPU.

### Triage
1. Check whether steal is isolated to one VM (likely a noisy neighbour on that host) or spread across several VMs in the zone (possible GCE infrastructure event).
2. Correlate with `instance/interruption_count`: recent live migrations can temporarily raise wait time.
3. Check application latency on the affected VMs; steal directly inflates request latency even when CPU utilisation looks normal.

### Remediation
For an isolated VM, stopping and starting it (not rebooting) moves it to a different host. For sole-tenant nodes, review the CPU overcommit ratio. If the zone shows a widespread pattern, check the Google Cloud status dashboard and open a support case.

### Tuning
Shared-core VMs (reserved cores below visible vCPUs) are excluded because throttling is expected. Adjust `steal_pct >= 10` and `affected_instances >= 1`. GCP Cloud Monitoring metrics typically arrive several minutes late, so the most recent minutes of the lookback window may be empty; the window is sized to tolerate this.
